purpose: DMSO is used to help relieve the pain and discomfort caused by a bladder condition called interstitial cystitis, which causes chronic bladder pain and pressure. It is placed directly into the bladder by a healthcare provider through a small tube called a catheter. It helps reduce inflammation and irritation inside the bladder.
how_it_works: DMSO works by reducing inflammation and swelling inside the bladder lining, which helps calm the pain signals coming from that area. It also has properties that help it penetrate tissues deeply, allowing it to work right where the problem is. Think of it like a soothing anti-inflammatory treatment applied directly to the irritated bladder wall.
common_side_effects: The most noticeable side effect is a garlic-like or oyster-like smell on your breath and skin that can last up to 72 hours after treatment — this is harmless but very common. You may also feel some temporary burning, stinging, or discomfort in the bladder right after the treatment. Mild nausea or headache can also occur.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as DMSO should be used with caution in these situations. Do not use if you have a urinary tract infection before treatment, as your doctor will want to treat the infection first. Regular eye exams may be recommended with long-term use since DMSO has rarely been associated with eye lens changes in animal studies.
typical_dosing: A healthcare provider instills 50 mL of the DMSO solution directly into your bladder through a catheter, and you hold it there for about 15 minutes before releasing it. Treatments are typically given every one to two weeks for several sessions, and your doctor will decide on the schedule that is best for you.
